title: Mixed native-immigrant founding teams show a firm-level complementarity in U.S. startup outcomes
source_unit: NBER Working Paper 33804 using linked U.S. startup, founder, employee, education, employment, funding, and exit records
geography: United States; startups and founders observed through linked administrative and commercial records

observations.period: Startup founding and outcomes three years after founding; paper issued May 2025

denominator.unit: U.S. startups with linked founder, employee, education, employment, funding, and exit histories; exact abstract denominator not disclosed

team_outperformance.value: native-immigrant founding teams outperform native-only and immigrant-only teams

employment_three_years.unit: startup employment three years after founding relative to native-only and immigrant-only teams

funding_access.value: more likely to secure funding and access larger funding rounds
funding_access.unit: startup financing outcome relative to comparison founding teams

exit_success.unit: startup exit outcome relative to comparison founding teams

proposed_mechanisms.value: diverse labor pools, access to successful venture capitalists, and expanded product markets
proposed_mechanisms.unit: mechanisms associated with native-immigrant team outperformance

instrumental_variables_check.value: native-immigrant teams remain larger and more likely to receive funding
instrumental_variables_check.unit: instrumental-variables robustness pattern using native shares in university-degree programs

observations.method: Linked startup records to founders' and employees' employment and education histories, compared native-only, immigrant-only, and mixed native-immigrant founding teams, and used an instrumental-variables strategy based on native shares in university-degree programs.
observations.uncertainty: The NBER paper is a working paper. The abstract does not disclose the exact linked sample denominator or every outcome definition. Team composition is not the same as immigrant status alone, and the evidence does not establish that every mixed team benefits, that the proposed mechanisms are individually identified, or that gains reach workers, consumers, or local communities.
observations.subgroup: Native-only, immigrant-only, and mixed native-immigrant founding teams; startup outcomes vary by sector, founder background, labor market, product market, financing network, and place.
observations.counterinterpretation: Mixed teams may differ in unobserved founder selection, education, networks, sector choice, legal or capital access, or willingness to seek funding. The instrumental-variables design strengthens the comparison but does not by itself establish equal causal contributions from labor-pool diversity, venture-capital access, or product-market expansion.

related_sources.claim: Official NBER DOI identifies the working paper.

boundary: This record measures a bounded firm-level complementarity between native and immigrant founders in U.S. startups. It does not establish a universal immigrant entrepreneurship effect, worker bargaining power, wage gains, consumer welfare, community spillovers, or a complete causal account of the mechanisms behind the observed startup outcomes.
